paper_metadata.title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
paper_metadata.author: Morten Magnusson

G_N_pc_kms_Msun.description: Gravitational constant in convenient galactic units

sample.source: SPARC (Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves)

key_equations.eq1_effective_energy_field: E_f = rho * (1 - S), where S in [0,1]

spearman_rho.description: Correlation between structural complexity (latent field proxy) and EFC performance

lsb_dwarf_success_rate.description: 100% success rate for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies

barred_spiral_performance.description: Systematically underperforms for structurally complex systems such as barred spirals

threshold_L_proxy.description: Default boundary between flow-dominated and latent-significant regimes (dimensionless latent field proxy)

flow_dominated.description: EFC applies without correction; LSB and diffuse dwarfs

latent_significant.description: EFC requires latent field correction; barred spirals and structurally complex systems

entropy_field.description: Normalised entropy field; S=0 means all energy is in flow, S=1 means fully thermalised

related_work.fire_simulations: EFC-R regime-dependent pattern aligns with FIRE hydrodynamical simulations showing non-equilibrium effects in dwarf galaxy evolution
